extraction.summary_en: This filing bundles two procès-verbaux for ARCHEAN TECHNOLOGIES: an AGE of 8 August 2005 (president's resignation, ratification of a share-transfer protocol whereby Malik GUELLATI, Christophe LEROUX and Marielle ROUJEAN sold the totality of their shares, resulting in a new 3-way split among BLANCO/AUMONT/GICQUEL, plus ratification of an agreement with ARCHEAN INTERNATIONAL) and an AGO of 2 September 2005 (appointment of Xavier AUMONT as new president, further resignation as directeur général). No capital increase or decrease is described anywhere in the OCR text, despite the registry label mentioning "Augmentation du capital social" — this is flagged as an issue since no such resolution or updated-statutes capital figure appears in the provided text. Share capital remains stated at 150,000 euros / 1,500 shares throughout.

issues: The registry labels this filing 'Augmentation du capital social', but no capital-increase resolution or updated capital figure appears anywhere in the OCR text provided; the capital is stated at 150,000 euros / 1,500 shares both before and after the events described. Possibly a companion document (updated statutes) not fully captured in this OCR, or a mislabelled registry entry.

The post-transfer répartition table is OCR-garbled in row order (names, share counts and percentages appear on separate lines out of sequence). Arithmetic check: 823+617+60=1500 (consistent with total), but 60/1500=4.00%, not the '6,00%' printed next to Franck GICQUEL — likely an OCR digit error (4 read as 6).

The document does not state the pre-transfer share allocation (i.e., how many shares each of GUELLATI, LEROUX and ROUJEAN held, nor whether BLANCO/AUMONT/GICQUEL already held shares before or GICQUEL was a new entrant), nor which specific buyer received each seller's shares. Individual SHAREHOLDER_SHARE_TRANSFER (seller,buyer,shares) records could not be constructed with confidence; only the resulting SHAREHOLDER_END for the three sellers and the post-transfer snapshot are recorded.
